activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Probabilities With Continuous Random Variables

feedback.problem:
Compute $P(1<X<2)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{20}{x}^{3},\, & 1\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X<2) & ={\int }_{1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{20}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{80}{x}^{4}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{80}(16-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
